findings.title: createdReceipt replay is not matter-scope-bound at the service layer
findings.violated_requirement: One idempotency key identifies exactly one command (contract §2.1); a reused key must retain its operation, matter and complete row intent
findings.location: apps/backend/internal/core/service/evidence_service.go:63-95 (createdReceipt replay path; Receipt lookup scoped (actor_id, idempotency_key) only — matter.sql FindReceipt, memory.go:443)
findings.tenant_boundary: Matter-level command identity inside one actor's key space
findings.caller_prerequisites: The SAME actor must hold active membership in two matters and resend the same idempotency key + identical fingerprint hash to the second matter
findings.source_sink: createdReceipt: tx.Receipt(actor,key) hit → rcpt.RequestHash == hash → returns matter A's stored CreatedSnapshot for the matter B command; no comparison of rcpt.MatterID/ScopeKind against the current env.header.MatterID
findings.expected: A receipt minted for matter A must not satisfy a command addressed to matter B; outcome should be ErrIdempotencyKeyReuse (or scope-mismatch refusal)
findings.observed: Service-level replay: matter B CreateGrid returned matter A's grid id (probe log on memory AND PostgreSQL)
findings.reproducer: SuiteAuditCrossScope 'same actor and key with a different matter hash must not replay matter A's receipt' (audit_cross_scope.go, isolated copy)
findings.impact: No cross-actor or cross-tenant data exposure (the replayed receipt is the actor's own object); a client reusing keys across matters gets a foreign-matter id under another matter's URL, corrupting command/audit identity
findings.mitigation_present: The product HTTP boundary mitigates: request fingerprint includes the URL path (server.go:345-347), so the same body under another matter hashes differently → ErrIdempotencyKeyReuse; the frontend mints a fresh key per intent and never reuses keys across scopes
findings.smallest_fix: In createdReceipt, before replaying: if rcpt.ScopeKind == ScopeMatter && (rcpt.MatterID == nil || *rcpt.MatterID != env.header.MatterID) → ErrIdempotencyKeyReuse; add a memory+PG contract regression (promote the audit probe)
findings.owner: Local Codex (primary backend remediation owner); reviewer-provided probe ready to promote

findings.title: Local people directory is issuer-wide, not organization-scoped
findings.violated_requirement: PO-authorized bounded LOCAL/DEV scope only; production needs an organization boundary (port/identity.go:55-56 says so itself)
findings.tenant_boundary: Identity discovery across would-be customer organizations sharing one IdP issuer
findings.caller_prerequisites: MC_LOCAL_PEOPLE_DIRECTORY=true AND actor is an ACTIVE workspace OWNER; query param q (≤100 chars)
findings.source_sink: SELECT users WHERE u.idp_issuer = actor.idp_issuer AND name substring match, excluding existing members, LIMIT 20
findings.observed: All users provisioned under the same issuer are discoverable regardless of any organization grouping; ZITADEL Organization claims are not consulted
findings.reproducer: Source-path proof; no runtime IdP in this review
findings.impact: If ever deployed multi-company on one issuer, an OWNER of any workspace can enumerate every other company's provisioned people by name
findings.mitigation_present: Flag defaults false (absent flag → uniform 404); in-code comment declares local/dev-only; audit of the flag boundary matches the PO authorization
findings.smallest_fix: Production gating: refuse the flag outside local/dev config profiles (startup validation), and replace with organization-scoped discovery when multi-tenancy ships

findings.title: No organization/customer entity exists: tenancy = Workspace (+ confidential Matter), with a global users table
findings.violated_requirement: Headline question: suitability for multiple independent customer organizations
findings.tenant_boundary: Workspace is the de-facto customer boundary; Matters are confidentiality sub-scopes
findings.source_sink: users(id, idp_issuer, idp_subject) is global across all workspaces; one person may hold memberships in any number of workspaces; no org entity, no org-scoped uniqueness beyond (issuer,sub), no org lifecycle/backup isolation
findings.expected: For independent customer firms today: one Workspace per customer firm works for logical confidentiality; organization-level SaaS isolation (lifecycle, billing, residency, per-org crypto/backup) is NOT modeled
findings.observed: Logical confidentiality holds end to end at Workspace/Matter level; organization semantics are absent by design
findings.reproducer: Schema reading; adversarial matrix T-03/T-06/T-10 all pass at workspace level
findings.impact: Suitable for the current single-issuer P0 deployment model; NOT a substitute for org-level SaaS tenancy if independent firms ever share an issuer (compounds A-02)
findings.mitigation_present: PO-approved P0 scope; the permission baseline (ws membership AND matter membership AND role) is enforced and tested
findings.smallest_fix: When multi-customer SaaS is approved: add Organization entity + org-scoped identity directory; keep Workspace as the operational boundary
findings.owner: PO / architecture decision (not an implementation defect for P0)

findings.title: No database row-level security; all isolation is application-enforced
findings.location: migrations 0001-0008 (no CREATE POLICY / RLS); stores rely on matter_id parameters
findings.caller_prerequisites: A future service/SQL bug would expose cross-matter rows with no DB backstop
findings.source_sink: Single shared schema; every query filters matter_id/workspace_id by parameter
findings.expected: Application isolation is demonstrably correct today (656-test suite + probes); RLS absence alone is not a critical finding per the audit rules
findings.mitigation_present: Composite FKs, append-only triggers, typed-totality constraint trigger, race-tested service locks
findings.smallest_fix: Defense-in-depth backlog: RLS keyed on a session GUC set per transaction, or per-tenant roles, when platform investment is approved

findings.title: Historical validation gaps on review history (0008): cell-scoped predecessor FK and question-revision FK remain missing
findings.violated_requirement: Review Matrix plan listed them as defense-in-depth minors
findings.location: migrations_mattercontrol/0008_review_matrix.sql (UNIQUE(supersedes_id) present; missing cell-scoped predecessor FK / question-revision FK — already ruled by the verifier as not a reproduced bypass because the unconditional Matter lock serializes commands)
findings.caller_prerequisites: Direct DB writes outside the service (none exist in product code)
findings.observed: Unchanged in the candidate; service-level guards hold
findings.mitigation_present: Service CAS + matter lock + race tests
findings.smallest_fix: Next schema migration (requires a PO-approved schema-change decision, not this review)
